This is experimental candidate evaluation, not industrial deployment or environmental-safety validation.
ai_technology: Org-Mol 3D molecular transformer
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary preprint abstract and version history

title: Machine-learning-guided lysine dioxygenase variant improves turnover
summary: A structure-based machine-learning mutation-ranking method, combined with molecular dynamics and human rational design, guided variant selection for a lysine dioxygenase. The authors report a five-substitution variant with total turnover number 218 ± 3, compared with 160 ± 2 for wild type in the reported assay. The improvement is specific to this enzyme and assay, not a claim of industrial or therapeutic performance. The source uses conflicting variant abbreviations: its abstract says LPNYI and its Results say LPYNI.
ai_technology: MutComputeX; molecular dynamics
organization: University of Minnesota Twin Cities; University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary preprint version and journal methods/results; the variant abbreviation differs between abstract and Results.

title: UniKP prioritizes a sulfotransferase for sulfotyrosine production
summary: UniKP was used to rank sulfotransferase homologues by predicted kinetics. The study reports experimental testing of five prioritized candidates and identifies EfST1A1, with about 6.5-fold higher in-vitro activity than the initial hit under the reported assay. Later directed evolution is not attributed to the model. This is a bounded enzyme-discovery result, not proof of industrial production or broad enzyme generality.
ai_technology: UniKP kinetic prediction
organization: Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: Publisher article preview/indexed text and institute source; full publisher text inaccessible. Issue date is recorded; exact online-first and earlier version not established.

title: AI-guided mining identifies and engineers an alkaline xylanase
summary: A fine-tuned sequence model and generative workflow guided identification of xylanase 8E20 and mutant 8E20-178. The abstract reports an optimum-pH shift from 8 to 10 and a 1.9-fold improvement, but calls the metric catalytic activity while the conclusion text calls it catalytic efficiency, so which one improved is unclear. Assay conditions and industrial-scale performance are not reported.
ai_technology: AAEPre sequence model; xynODM generative model
organization: Institute of Animal Science, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary source checked for identity, publication date, AI workflow and the bounded experimental result stated.

title: Topological learning and simulations predict lithium superionic-conductor candidates
summary: A multiscale topological-learning workflow combined algebraic-topology descriptors, unsupervised clustering and ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations to screen lithium-containing structures. The study reports 14 candidate conductors meeting computational thresholds for diffusion barriers and electrochemical stability. The reported conductivities are simulated, with ambient values estimated from elevated-temperature trajectories. Some candidates had prior experimental reports or patents cited by the authors; those are not experimental validation produced by this AI workflow. Many candidates remain untested.
ai_technology: Multiscale topological learning; persistent homology; affinity propagation clustering; ab initio molecular dynamics
organization: Peking University; Michigan State University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text and publication metadata; article identity, methods, bounded computational outcomes and affiliation block.

title: Machine learning and genetic search predict stronger refractory alloys
summary: A random-forest model trained on published refractory high-entropy-alloy data was coupled to a stochastic genetic algorithm to optimize alloy compositions for yield strength at selected temperatures. For an AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr base composition, the authors report modeled gains of 90 MPa at 25 °C and 13% at 1,000 °C for optimized compositions. Other base-alloy optimizations are also reported. The proposed alloys were not experimentally fabricated or mechanically measured in this study; these are computational design predictions.
ai_technology: Random-forest regression; stochastic genetic algorithm
organization: CFD Research Corporation; University at Buffalo

source_review.scope: Research Square primary v1 full text and posted-date metadata

title: Mass spectrometry and machine learning identify bioactive peptide NHPD-50
summary: A predicted-peptide-variant model trained using mass-spectrometry observations from seven mouse tissues helped prioritize candidate peptides. The authors report that NHPD-50, a secretogranin-1-derived peptide, lowered blood glucose and increased plasma insulin in specified diabetic-mouse experiments. The authors state that the data do not establish the peptide’s exact mechanism. These are early preclinical findings, not a human diabetes treatment; other predicted peptides had different or absent outcomes.
ai_technology: Predicted-peptide-variant machine-learning prioritization from mass-spectrometry data
organization: Novo Nordisk A/S

source_review.scope: Primary Nature full article and bibliographic metadata reviewed for identity, AI role, date, affiliation and bounded mouse results.

title: Machine learning simulations reveal nonequilibrium short-range order in metallic alloys
summary: A moment-tensor machine-learning interatomic potential enabled large-scale simulations of CrCoNi processing. The authors report that thermomechanical deformation and solidification can generate steady-state chemical short-range order outside the equilibrium-annealing spectrum, and propose an ordering-bias mechanism. This is a simulation-based computational finding, not direct experimental validation of the predicted states in manufactured alloys. The result and AI role were already present in arXiv v1; journal publication followed in 2025.
ai_technology: Moment-tensor machine-learning interatomic potential; E(3)-equivariant graph neural network for local chemical-motif identification
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text and submission history; indexed Nature Communications full text including Methods/contributions and affiliation block; PubMed metadata/abstract.

title: MutexaGPT-guided cold-adapted amylase variants
summary: The MutexaGPT multi-agent large language model system translated a cold-adaptation design request into molecular simulations and linker-variant proposals for bidomain amylase. The authors report experimentally validated variants with 1.7-fold and 3.7-fold activity enhancement at 0 °C. The preprint appeared on 19 June 2026; the peer-reviewed journal version followed on 10 September 2026.
ai_technology: Multi-agent large language model system coordinating high-throughput molecular dynamics simulations and mutation design
organization: Vanderbilt University

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text indexed content and metadata; primary Nature Computational Science indexed article text, including abstract, Methods, experimental result, date and affiliation block.

title: EvoGradient evolves antimicrobial peptides active against resistant pathogens
summary: EvoGradient uses an explainable deep-learning potency model and virtual sequence evolution to optimize candidate antimicrobial peptides. Applied to peptides encoded by low-abundance human oral bacteria, it virtually evolved 32 candidates; the six most effective were synthesized and tested against multidrug-resistant pathogens. The authors report activity across carbapenem-resistant E. coli, K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii and vancomycin-resistant E. faecium; pep-19-mod reduced bacterial loads by more than 95% in mouse thigh-infection models under the reported systemic and local administrations. These are preclinical findings and do not establish human efficacy or safety.
ai_technology: Explainable deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide potency model with gradient-based virtual sequence evolution
organization: Southeast University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Microbiology indexed article text and primary PubMed abstract/metadata/affiliations; conclusions limited to reported preclinical assays.

title: HydrAMP generates antimicrobial peptide analogues validated in bacterial assays
summary: HydrAMP, a conditional variational autoencoder with antimicrobial activity classifiers, generated peptide analogues and de novo candidates. The 2022 preprint reports wet-lab confirmation of increased activity for a generated Pexiganan-based analogue; the 2023 journal version reports testing across five bacterial strains, including nine analogues of clinical prototypes and six analogues of an inactive peptide. The tested panel was small and model/human filtered; it does not establish therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder with classifier-guided peptide generation and molecular-dynamics-based candidate preselection
organization: University of Warsaw

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 abstract/metadata; primary Nature Communications indexed full article including methods/results; primary publisher author correction.

title: Offline reinforcement learning identifies an AgBiI4 film-processing condition
summary: The Daisy framework combines SEM-image interpretation with offline reinforcement learning trained on historical Ag-Bi-I thin-film conditions and microstructure measurements. For AgBiI4, the planner proposed a condition outside the recorded combinations, and a newly fabricated film showed no visible pinholes and mean grain size 14.5% above the historical mean for defect-free samples. Its grain distribution was comparable to the best historical sample, so the study does not show that the new condition outperformed the previous best or improved device performance.
ai_technology: Daisy image-analysis models and offline reinforcement-learning synthesis planner trained on historical microstructure data
organization: University of Washington

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text as indexed, including article date, methods, results, author contributions and affiliations.

title: A chemical foundation model guides high-conductivity electrolyte formulation
summary: Researchers fine-tuned the SMI-TED chemical foundation model on 13,666 literature measurements of ionic conductivity and screened 100,000 generated electrolyte formulations. Sixteen selected formulations were measured experimentally, with seven exceeding 10 mS/cm. A model-generated LiFSI formulation measured 19.14 mS/cm at room temperature, 82% above the best literature value in the paper’s comparison; the model had predicted 10.52 mS/cm. Conductivity is only one electrolyte property and does not establish electrochemical stability, safety or battery performance. The article was published 2025-08-30; a later correction changed an author name only.
ai_technology: SMI-TED chemical foundation model fine-tuned for electrolyte mixture ionic-conductivity prediction and generative screening
organization: IBM Research

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text including methods, measured outcomes, affiliations and publication date; primary publisher correction.

title: Active learning identifies high-performing electrolyte solvents for anode-free lithium metal cells
summary: Researchers used sequential Bayesian experimental design with Bayesian model averaging to select electrolyte solvents for testing in Cu||LiFePO4 cells, feeding cycle-capacity results back into the model over seven campaigns. The study reports seven top-performing solvent electrolytes and says four distinct solvents rival state-of-the-art performance; three were previously unreported as electrolytes for anode-free cells. Five of nine compounds tested in the final batch exceeded 100 mAh/g discharge capacity at cycle 20. The result is limited to the tested cell configuration and cycling conditions and does not establish commercial battery performance.
ai_technology: Active learning with sequential Bayesian experimental design, Bayesian model averaging and Gaussian-process surrogate models
organization: University of Chicago

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications full text as indexed; primary PMC text with methods/results/contributions; institutional full-paper manuscript mirror.

title: PhotoCat guides experimental discovery of photocatalytic reactions
summary: The PhotoCat Transformer was pretrained on general reaction data and fine-tuned on the authors’ photocatalysis database to predict products and reaction conditions. In the 2023 ChemRxiv version, the authors report using it to guide experimental validation of previously unreported photocatalytic reactions. The later 2026 journal version describes four novel validated reactions, whereas the preprint reports five; this entry makes no exact-count claim and treats the journal article as a revised version of the same study.
ai_technology: Transformer-based deep-learning reaction predictor pretrained on USPTO and fine-tuned on PhotoCatDB, with reaction-condition inputs
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v2 full-text PDF and version-history metadata; primary PMC full-text journal version and publication metadata. The preprint and journal versions report different counts (five versus four); the summary preserves this discrepancy.

title: Machine learning screening identifies an efficient molecular photocatalytic CO2-reduction system
summary: A machine-learning-accelerated descriptor workflow screened 3,444 molecular photosensitizer–catalyst systems, including 180,000 conformations, and selected six candidates for experimental validation. The primary article reports that the optimal tested system reached a turnover number of 4,390 and uses time-resolved spectroscopy and first-principles calculations to examine dipole coupling. The reported outcome is bounded to the tested system and the study’s screening scope.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening using descriptors for photosensitization, electron transfer, and catalysis
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Catalysis indexed article text, abstract, extended-data descriptions, metadata and affiliation block; institutional research announcement checked as corroboration.

title: Machine learning-guided synthesis of two-dimensional AgBi iodide perovskites
summary: The authors combined an 80-amine high-throughput synthesis dataset, chemistry-informed molecular descriptors, subgroup discovery and a support-vector classifier to rank organic spacers for 2D AgBi iodide perovskites. Of 13 model-selected candidates taken forward, eight were successfully synthesized and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction. The study reports a 61.5% success rate in this selected validation set; it does not establish universal synthesis performance across other perovskite families.
ai_technology: Subgroup discovery and support-vector classification using physicochemical and molecular-topology descriptors
organization: Southeast University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications publisher PDF indexed full text including Results, Methods, author contributions and article metadata; Southeast University institutional announcement checked for corroboration.

title: Deep learning identifies antimicrobial peptides hidden in prion-related proteins
summary: APEX 1.1 screened 19.3 million peptide fragments from 2,897 prion-related proteins and identified 1,179 candidate antimicrobial peptides, termed prionins. Among 75 synthesized candidates, 59 inhibited at least one tested bacterial strain; two selected peptides reduced Acinetobacter baumannii burden in a mouse skin-abscess model. The study shows that prion-related sequences can yield experimentally active antimicrobial fragments, but does not show that these peptides are naturally released or function as host-defense agents in their source organisms.
ai_technology: APEX 1.1 deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide prediction and prioritization
organization: University of Pennsylvania

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Microbiology full text as indexed, including methods, results, author contributions and affiliations.

title: Machine learning screening identifies GW3965 activity against invasive group A Streptococcus
summary: A neural network trained on measured growth responses from 2,560 compounds screened 6,111 FDA-evaluated compounds for activity against multidrug-resistant emm92 group A Streptococcus. Of nine selected compounds tested, GW3965 reduced bacterial survival by 99% at an MIC of 6.25 μM. The authors also report improved wound closure in an infected human skin-equivalent model and reduced lesion area and bacterial burden in mice. This is preclinical evidence and does not establish efficacy or safety in people. The peer-reviewed journal article followed on 2026-05-30 and reports the same core GW3965 result.
ai_technology: Deep neural network trained on compound SMILES and measured bacterial growth responses; model screened an FDA-evaluated compound library
organization: West Virginia University

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text PDF, including posted date, affiliations, Methods and experimental outcomes; primary Nature publisher indexed article text and journal-version abstract/results.

title: AI-assisted analysis reveals retrospective seismicity before the Dingri earthquake
summary: A PhaseNet-assisted workflow combined phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching on records from one permanent station to reconstruct seismicity in the two years before the 2025 Mw 7.1 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock. This retrospective pattern is interpreted as compatible with late-stage nucleation; the study does not establish a prospective earthquake forecast.
ai_technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker combined with polarisation analysis and template matching
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS)

source_review.scope: Primary Scientific Reports indexed article, including abstract, Methods, Results, article dates and author-affiliation block.

title: Machine-learning seismic catalogue reveals a long-period swarm before Sierra Negra eruption onset
summary: A machine-learning phase-picking and template-matching workflow expanded the catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset, identifying a northwestern-caldera swarm of long-period microearthquakes missing from earlier manually picked records. The authors report the swarm began about two hours after a Mw 5.4 intra-caldera earthquake and preceded edifice failure and magma intrusion. The proposed fluid-triggering sequence is an interpretation of retrospective seismic and geodetic observations, not a prospective eruption forecast.
ai_technology: Volpick EQTransformer-based seismic phase picker combined with template matching and geodetic analysis
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed article text and PDF-indexed article content, including abstract, Results, Methods, metadata and author-affiliation section.

title: Experimental feedback guides ESM-2 to brighter CreiLOV variants
summary: Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF) used a learned fluorescence reward model to align ESM-2 with measured CreiLOV sequence-function data. In the peer-reviewed study, the authors expressed 60 generated variants in E. coli and measured cellular fluorescence; six of ten aligned ESM-2 five-mutant designs exceeded CreiLOV fluorescence, and three aligned designs exceeded CreiLOV-T7S. The first bioRxiv version (posted 2025-05-08) already described experimentally enhanced fluorescence from RLXF-aligned designs; detailed measurements here are from the 2026 journal version. The earlier ICLR workshop comparison was computational and did not report new wet-lab fluorescence assays.
ai_technology: 650-million-parameter ESM-2 protein language model aligned by reinforcement learning from experimental feedback using a learned sequence-fluorescence reward model
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 abstract, posting-date and affiliation metadata; primary GEM@ICLR workshop paper full text for methods and experimental outcomes; primary Nature Communications indexed text for later journal-version comparison.

title: A biophysics-informed protein language model designs functional GFP variants
summary: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL) combines transformer pretraining on simulated protein biophysics with fine-tuning on experimental sequence–function data. Using only 64 experimental GFP examples, the authors designed 20 previously untested variants and measured their fluorescence; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, although none was brighter than wild-type GFP. The result demonstrates functional design under a small-data setup, not improved brightness over wild type. The result was present in the bioRxiv version posted 2024-03-17; the GEM@ICLR 2024 workshop paper provides the detailed 20-variant assay report, and the later journal version is the same study.
ai_technology: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL), a transformer protein language model pretrained on simulated biophysical features and fine-tuned on experimental data
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 indexed abstract, posting date and affiliation metadata; primary GEM@ICLR workshop paper full text with methods and experimental outcomes.

title: Machine learning guides engineering of an alkaloid-biosynthesis enzyme
summary: Researchers developed MutComputeX, a structure-based residual neural network for assessing amino-acid substitutions in protein–ligand environments, and used it with a 4′-O-methylnorbelladine biosensor to engineer the plant methyltransferase Nb4OMT in Escherichia coli. The paper reports engineered variants with 60% higher product titer, twofold higher catalytic activity, threefold lower off-product regioisomer formation and 5 °C higher thermostability; ligand-aware predictions helped identify the beneficial A53M substitution. These enzyme and product results do not demonstrate complete microbial production of galantamine.
ai_technology: MutComputeX structure-based residual neural network for protein–ligand mutation design
organization: University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications full text as indexed, including methods/results, author contributions and affiliation block.

title: Similarity-informed machine learning guides experimental high-entropy alloy catalyst discovery
summary: A graph neural network augmented with quantum-inspired adsorption-site similarity reduced the DFT training data needed for a given prediction accuracy from 1,600 to 800 calculations. The model identified a five-metal Fe–Co–Ni–Ir–Ru high-entropy alloy candidate for oxygen reduction; the author group reports experimental validation and performance above a Pt/C comparison. The publisher abstract gives a predicted overpotential of 0.24 V, which is not presented here as the measured value. This is a laboratory catalyst result, not a fuel-cell deployment claim.
ai_technology: Similarity-augmented graph neural network for adsorption-site and alloy-composition screening
organization: Computational Laboratory for Energy and Nanoscience

source_review.scope: Primary ScienceDirect indexed abstract and metadata; primary author-group publication page. Direct publisher full-text open was blocked, so no full Methods or complete article affiliation review is claimed.

title: HydrAMP-guided design of short tryptophan-rich antimicrobial peptides
summary: HydrAMP generated analogues from a short Arg/Trp prototype, with AMPlify scoring and empirical filters used to select candidates. The authors synthesized three peptides and measured antimicrobial activity across bacterial strains; AMP3 showed the broadest activity among those tested, including MIC50 values of 15 μM against E. coli and 125 μM against P. aeruginosa. This is a small, model-assisted peptide panel built on a known sequence motif, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: HydrAMP deep-learning peptide sequence generator and AMPlify deep-learning antimicrobial-activity scorer
organization: University of Napoli Federico II

source_review.scope: Primary Wiley publisher full-text indexed article including sequences, Methods, MIC results and publication date; PubMed metadata/abstract/affiliation; separate primary Nature Communications article reviewed to compare the prior HydrAMP wet-lab prototypes and results.

title: Uni-Mol screening guides experimental validation of β-sheet tetrapeptide assemblies
summary: A fine-tuned Uni-Mol model used simulation-derived data to screen 160,000 tetrapeptides. Researchers experimentally tested 26 selected tetrapeptide candidates: 15 formed β-sheet assemblies, including seven hydrogelators, as assessed with structural and assembly assays. The study reports experimental validation across 46 candidates overall; the 15/26 result is specific to the screened tetrapeptide set. This is a materials-science preprint, not evidence of medical function or clinical use. A related 2023 study explored tetrapeptide hydrogelation; this record makes no claim that every sequence is unprecedented and is limited to the present paper’s β-sheet structural validation.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Uni-Mol machine-learning model for Amyloid-Like Tendency prediction, guided by hybrid-resolution molecular-dynamics simulations
organization: Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School

source_review.scope: ChemRxiv v1 page, full manuscript and Supplementary Information; official bioRxiv API metadata/abstract for cited 2025 computational preprint; primary 2023 hydrogel paper and linked supplementary-data index. Full-text source limits and the bounded result are stated.

title: Iterative Gaussian process screening discovers selective aurein-derived antifungal peptides
summary: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression workflow iteratively selected 23 synthetic α/β-peptide analogues for synthesis and measurements of fungal inhibition and human-red-blood-cell hemolysis. One lead, peptide 6-4, was a measured variant of an existing aurein-derived template and achieved a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval) versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2. Its high selectivity was driven by low hemolysis; the result is a specific peptide-design and assay contribution, not a new peptide scaffold or evidence of therapeutic efficacy. The ChemRxiv v1 result was posted on 2024-10-04; the peer-reviewed journal article followed in 2025.
ai_technology: Iterative uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression using molecular descriptors and measured antifungal/hemolysis labels
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv version-history record and v2 manuscript; primary RSC indexed full article PDF, including sequence tables, Results, Methods and publication metadata; PubMed primary abstract/affiliation metadata.

title: Family-specific machine learning prioritizes enzyme variants for prospective testing
summary: Researchers screened 1,513 natural SGNH-hydrolase homologues and trained task-specific sequence CNNs on the resulting activity, thermostability, and substrate-preference data. The models helped select candidates for a prospective 230-sequence assay panel, where CNN-selected candidates were enriched for target traits relative to generalist pretrained and physics-based baselines; the panel also included other selection strategies and random controls. Assays used clarified E. coli lysates and measured relative maximum velocity, integrating expression and catalysis. The first public version with this result was posted to bioRxiv on 2026-06-03; a Research Square version followed on 2026-06-05.
ai_technology: Task-specific convolutional neural networks trained on amino-acid sequences; CNN-based HEV and UCB selection strategies
organization: CSIRO Environment

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text as indexed, including title, posting date, affiliations, methods, prospective assay results and limitations; primary Research Square v1 identity/date record.

title: Machine-learning screening guides ionic-liquid polymer electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries
summary: A machine-learning and quantum-chemistry workflow screened ionic liquids for conductivity and electrochemical-window properties, then guided selection for rigid-rod polyelectrolyte membranes. The 2022 preprint reports ~50 μm membranes and lithium-cell testing, including symmetric-cell cycling up to 800 hours at room temperature and reversible operation at 6 mA cm−2 at 80°C. Its preprint abstract reports 146 mAh g−1 at 5C/80°C; the later 2023 journal abstract lists 3C, so those version-specific figures are not conflated.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural network and ensemble SVM/random-forest/XGBoost screening with Psi4 quantum-chemistry descriptors
organization: Fudan University

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text PDF, including version date, affiliations, Methods and Results; primary Nature Communications journal article indexed text and metadata; primary publisher correction notice.

title: Machine-learning screening identifies bacterial-selective membrane-active compounds
summary: The June 2026 bioRxiv version describes an initial machine-learning-guided screen of ZINC20 compounds balancing predicted antibacterial activity, mammalian-cell toxicity, and mechanism-of-action novelty. Among 61 purchased candidates, six showed partial growth inhibition; 49 were non-toxic to HepG2 cells at 50 μM. Flow cytometry indicated membrane disruption for four of the six initial active hits and membrane depolarization for two. A September version reports additional screening and revised models; its expanded results are not attributed to the June version here. The study does not report a novel protein target or clinical antibiotic.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural networks for antibacterial activity/toxicity with XGBoost mechanism-of-action classification and novelty filtering
organization: Princeton University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC-indexed full text for the June bioRxiv v1, primary PubMed preprint abstract/metadata, and primary PMC/PubMed metadata for the later September version to distinguish version-specific results.

title: Machine-learning screening identifies two drug-repurposing candidates against tuberculosis
summary: A virtual-screening workflow combined XGBoost and graph-neural-network models to screen 11,576 DrugBank compounds. Researchers selected 15 candidates for evaluation; four met the study’s activity cutoff against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv. Aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin were further tested against multidrug-resistant isolates, intracellular bacteria and recombinant DNA gyrase. These are laboratory repurposing results, not evidence of patient benefit or clinical safety. A same-team patent-family publication predates the journal article; this record makes no priority claim over patent disclosures. Concentration values are omitted because of inconsistent units in the rendered tables.
ai_technology: Ensemble virtual screening with XGBoost and graph neural networks
organization: Institute for Artificial Intelligence & Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

source_review.scope: Primary Oxford Academic full indexed article, including abstract, Methods, results, article history and author affiliations; patent-family chronology checked from the patent family page. A-version patent text was not reviewed.

title: AI-assisted virtual screening identifies a dual-stage antimalarial candidate
summary: An AI-assisted virtual-screening cascade using shape-based and machine-learning models prioritized potential Plasmodium kinase inhibitors. Eight virtual hits were experimentally evaluated; LabMol-167 inhibited P. berghei ookinete conversion and P. falciparum blood-stage parasites at nanomolar concentrations and showed low cytotoxicity in mammalian cells. A possible additional PK5 target was proposed from computational target fishing and docking, not demonstrated experimentally. This is a preclinical hit result and does not establish therapeutic efficacy. The article appeared online on 2021-03-16.
ai_technology: AI-assisted virtual screening combining shape-based and machine-learning models
organization: Federal University of Goiás

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed abstract, publication metadata, and author-affiliation block; claim limited to the findings explicitly stated in the abstract.

title: Physics-informed machine learning guides experimental Curie-temperature validation in Ce–Zr–Fe alloys
summary: A machine-learning model trained on measured Curie temperatures selected two compositions in the (Zr1−xCex)Fe2 system, (Zr0.16Ce0.84)Fe2 and (Zr0.94Ce0.06)Fe2, for experimental validation. The study also reports a relationship between electronic states near the Fermi level and Curie temperature, including a breakdown of de Gennes scaling below a rare-earth-content threshold. This is a materials discovery study, not evidence of a finished permanent magnet or deployed technology.
ai_technology: Physics-informed machine-learning model trained on experimentally measured Curie temperatures
organization: Ames National Laboratory, U.S. Department of Energy; Iowa State University

title: Bayesian optimization identifies a methane-combustion catalyst formula
summary: Bayesian optimization guided the experimental search over Pt/Pd and Ce/Zr ratios in PtPd@CeZrOx core–shell nanospheres. The authors report that two optimization rounds comprising 18 experiments found a formula with methane-conversion T50 approaching 330 °C, lower than prior reports cited by the study. The full assay conditions and comparison basis were not reviewed here; this is a bounded laboratory result, not a claim of general superiority, durability, or deployment.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization for experimental catalyst-formula selection
organization: Beihang University

title: Deep learning maps fine-scale plant distributions and fire-associated change
summary: DeepBiosphere combines a residual CNN trained on citizen-science observations with aerial imagery to map California distributions for 2,221 plant species. The authors report median AUC 0.95 versus 0.88 for climate-only models and use repeat imagery to map plant-community change associated with the 2013 Rim Fire. These are California-specific ecological maps and observational associations; the study does not establish causal effects of fire or a new species discovery.
ai_technology: DeepBiosphere residual convolutional neural network for species-distribution mapping
organization: Carnegie Science

title: Machine learning screening selects an energetic material for laboratory characterization
summary: A high-throughput workflow combined learned molecular-property predictions and crystal-packing classification to screen 25,112 generated structures and select ICM-104. The authors synthesized and characterized the selected material, reporting that its measured properties agreed with the model-assisted predictions. This is one laboratory-scale, study-specific material result; the broad candidate space remains computational, and the study does not establish scale-up, deployment or independent replication.

title: SLIDE links islet T-cell clone expansion to immune gene programs
summary: SLIDE, an interpretable latent-factor interaction method, was applied to paired single-cell RNA-seq and T-cell receptor data from islet-derived CD4 T cells in NOD mice. The analysis identified latent components associated with clonal expansion and grouped inhibitory-receptor and intracellular signaling/apoptosis-related genes among the associated programs. The result is an inference from existing multiomic data, not a causal perturbation; it is a distinct T1D application in the same article as the separately catalogued systemic-sclerosis analysis.

title: An attention-based neural network generates functional secretion signal peptides
summary: An attention-based Transformer trained on signal-peptide data from Swiss-Prot generated candidate secretion sequences. Experimental testing in an industrial Bacillus subtilis strain found that model-generated signal peptides directed secreted enzyme activity competitive with industrially used signal peptides. The result establishes functional candidates in the reported host and assay; it does not establish broad performance across proteins or production hosts. The primary institutional record gives the article publication date as 2020-07-10.

Held-out test set (MSE 0.0079; Pearson r=0.46) plus in-silico motif insertion/ablation; no direct experimental perturbation validation reported in the results.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network predicts chromatin co-accessibility maps from DNA sequence; interpretation provides motif-level regulatory hypotheses.
organization: Not stated in the reviewed material

source_review.scope: Read the full bioRxiv v1 preprint in PMC (2026-10-31). Methods/Results show ChAI-Net is a deep CNN trained on ~3.4 million 2,048-bp windows of mouse embryonic stem-cell SAMOSA single-molecule footprint data to predict 16-bp-resolution co-accessibility maps. Held-out testing reports MSE 0.0079 and Pearson r=0.46; model interpretation and in-silico motif insertion/ablation identify sequence motifs and spacing/orientation patterns associated with co-accessibility, including patterns not recovered by average-accessibility modeling. This is a new, model-derived regulatory finding, with validation limited to held-out data and computational perturbations in one cell context (not causal wet-lab perturbation). The full text identifies Version 1 dated 2026-10-31 as containing the result. Exact DOI and title were checked and are absent from the active and archived catalog snapshots.

title: A CNN search exposes a real false-positive ceiling and supports validation of TOI-6662 b

The work also applies candidate prioritization and follow-up to statistically validate TOI-6662 b. The validated planet is a specific astronomy result, while the small candidate sample and selection process limit generalization of the benchmark findings.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for TESS transit candidate detection

title: Planar energetics do not determine twin persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium
summary: Two learned potentials that reproduce similar planar slip energetics predicted markedly different retained twin coverage (64% versus 14%) from the same precursor under identical loading. The result is computational; no experimental confirmation is claimed.
ai_technology: A MACE-based machine-learned interatomic potential (Al-QP), trained on strain-coupled fault, twin, and interface configurations, enabled atomistic simulations of twin formation and persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium.

title: Cracking into RACS - I. Measuring the cosmic dipole in the RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 radio surveys with simulation-based inference
summary: Simulation-based inference applied to two Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey bands found radio-galaxy count dipoles inconsistent with the cosmic microwave background kinematic dipole. Warmer antennas were associated with lower reported flux densities. The inference depends on survey modeling and simulations.
ai_technology: A neural network in a simulation-based inference pipeline learned the likelihood function from simulated survey data, including a model of antenna-temperature effects on flux density.

title: AI-optimized magnetic nanobiocatalyst enables recyclable citrulline production
summary: A neural-network-assisted optimization selected a magnetic-nanoparticle formulation of arginine deiminase for citrulline production. title: Machine learning combines plasma spectroscopy and protein profiles for exploratory endometriosis classification
summary: A single-center study collected plasma from 37 participants with endometriosis and 45 with other benign gynecological disorders. Seventy had paired infrared-spectroscopy and HPLC protein-profile measurements. Feature selection and a shallow neural-network classifier using mid-level data fusion achieved reported sensitivity of 80% and ROC AUC of 0.80 in repeated held-out splits with nested tuning. In a separate protein-profile analysis, K-nearest-neighbor classification and SHAP prioritized a plasma fraction for mass spectrometry, identifying five candidate proteins. This is exploratory retrospective diagnostic evidence: the cohort was small, participant ages differed between groups, there was no independent external validation, and the proteins require orthogonal validation before being considered reliable biomarkers. The work does not establish a clinically validated diagnostic test or improved patient outcomes.

title: Transfer learning grades oral epithelial dysplasia in patient-level held-out histology images
summary: A retrospective study compared learned classifiers for four-grade oral epithelial dysplasia assessment using 3,777 histopathology tissue strips from 94 patients. title: Elastic-net analysis finds limited genomic separation of malaria infections in two connected Amazonian communities
summary: An exploratory preprint applied elastic-net logistic regression to existing genomic data from 47 Plasmodium vivax infections detected in two neighboring Peruvian Amazon communities, including 12 people reporting recent local travel. This supports a limited finding that fine-scale assignment was weak and sensitive to sample composition in this dataset. The analyses used different, overlapping infection sets, so their comparison does not isolate a causal effect of travel. Self-reported travel did not establish infection origin; intervals were conditional on saved predictions, and no independent cohort or operational surveillance benefit was tested.

title: Machine learning shows hepatocyte-like cell lines poorly reproduce primary liver enhancer activity
summary: The authors compared four immortalized hepatocyte-like cell lines with primary liver tissue using chromatin-accessibility assays, motif analysis and a previously trained multi-species liver-enhancer classifier. title: AlphaFold3-aided cryo-EM resolves native Anopheles salivary protein complexes
summary: Biochemical and mass-spectrometry analyses identified native interactions among Anopheles mosquito salivary proteins, including Saglin and SGS4/SGS5. summary: A preprint compared 101survival-model combinations across three public ovarian-cancer cohorts (107, 80 and 101 participants), selecting a five-gene model in which KIAA0408 had the largest coefficient. title: Machine-learning feature selection identifies student-performance factors in Nepal
summary: A study analyzed 1,021 survey responses from engineering students reflecting on their first year at colleges affiliated with Tribhuvan University in Nepal. A feature-selection vote including Random Forest and AdaBoost selected 21 candidate academic, psychometric and demographic factors, triangulated with 11 focus-group themes and expert review. The reported set included adaptation, motivation, residence and travel-time factors alongside academic measures. These context-dependent selections do not establish causal effects, externally validated predictive performance or transfer beyond the sampled institution system.
ai_technology: Random Forest and AdaBoost within a multi-method feature-selection vote
organization: Tribhuvan University

source_review.scope: Original journal PDF: posting and peer-review metadata, cohort/data collection, six-method feature-selection vote, triangulation, result categories and conclusions.

title: Patient-level tests evaluate a quantum-inspired transformer model for breast ultrasound lesion classification
summary: A classical GAN/vision-transformer system jointly segmented breast-ultrasound lesions and classified malignancy in two public clinical-image datasets. The paper reports patient-level separation and bidirectional BUSI/UDIAT cross-dataset F1 scores of 97.14% and 96.81%. This is retrospective evaluation of existing images, and the authors state that actual clinical conditions were not reproduced. Larger heterogeneous clinical populations and prospective workflow evaluation are needed; the quantum-inspired components do not establish physical quantum computation or advantage.
ai_technology: Quantum-inspired generative adversarial segmentation with a vision-transformer classification head
organization: Hindusthan Institute of Technology

source_review.scope: Publisher Article in Press PDF: dataset and patient-level split methods, architecture and learned operations, cross-dataset validation results, limitations and data-availability statement.

title: Multimodal language models extract seizure semiology and support patient-held-out seizure classification
summary: An October 2025 preprint analyzed 90 video-EEG-confirmed events from 29 patients at one epilepsy-monitoring unit using vision-language and audio-language models to extract clinical features. With leave-one-patient-out testing, KNN using automated features achieved F1 and AUC of 0.76, below the classifier using expert features. Automated feature extraction itself had mean F1 of 0.51 against expert annotations, and the small retrospective cohort does not establish clinical utility or external generalization. A later journal version was dated November 2026; the detailed results here describe the accessible preprint.
ai_technology: InternVL vision-language models and Qwen audio/vision-language models with downstream KNN and other classifiers
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; University of Alabama at Birmingham

source_review.scope: Europe PMC XML full text of medRxiv preprint, including methods, patient cohort, MLLM operations, LOPO protocol and results; publisher-deposited final journal abstract and DOI date metadata.

title: GWAS identifies a functional MSTN variant associated with higher lean mass in humans
summary: A genome-wide association meta-analysis of DXA-derived lean mass in about 79,000 people identified 63 loci, including a rare MSTN variant associated with higher leg lean mass. Supervised deep residual convolutional networks imputed missing DXA/MRI image-derived phenotypes from raw images for UK Biobank association analyses; statistical GWAS and researcher-led assays supplied the genetic and functional evidence. The findings are observational, largely from European-ancestry participants, and do not establish clinical benefit from myostatin inhibition.
ai_technology: Supervised deep residual convolutional neural networks for DXA/MRI image-derived phenotype imputation
organization: deCODE genetics

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, Results, UK Biobank imaging-processing Methods, Discussion limitations and publication metadata.

title: Learned expert skills improve shared control in a CT-guided biopsy robot
summary: A CT-guided biopsy robot used a variational autoencoder–hidden Markov model and dynamic motion primitives to learn procedural phases and trajectories from expert demonstrations. Its shared controller reduced interaction forces and targeting errors relative to manual, leader–follower and admittance control in phantom and rabbit experiments, with nine experiments per strategy; porcine work separately assessed robotic feasibility. These preclinical results do not establish safety or benefit in patients, and the learned skills came from a limited expert panel.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder–hidden Markov model and dynamic motion primitives for expert-skill learning
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, robot/control Results, expert-skill learning Methods and Discussion limitations, with phantom, rabbit and porcine distinctions checked.

title: Artificial neural network analysis links immersion with self-efficacy in VR upper-limb training
summary: Artificial neural networks analyzed self-reports from 280 healthy adults who used a VR upper-limb training system. With ten-fold cross-validation, the ANN analysis ranked immersion above learning motivation as a predictor of task-specific self-efficacy, while linear structural-equation analysis ranked learning motivation higher. This preprint reports associations in young adults from one city, without causal evidence or rehabilitation outcomes.
ai_technology: Artificial neural networks with 10-fold cross-validation
organization: Fujian University of Technology

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full-text PDF: abstract, participant Methods, ANN analysis, cross-validation and limitations; Crossref version/publication metadata.

title: Cohort audit finds unstable performance in efferocytosis-related prognostic scores
summary: A retrospective audit rebuilt an efferocytosis-related head-and-neck-cancer prognostic analysis in 519 primary tumors after detecting non-primary rows in the original cohort. A Cox-LASSO workflow selected a nine-gene sensitivity score, but its exact composition recurred in none of 500 full-pipeline bootstrap samples and repeated nested cross-validation yielded a mean C-index of 0.587. Survival associations persisted in some analyses while external performance was inconsistent, and a fixed cutoff did not transfer. The authors treat both this reconstruction and the historical six-gene score as hypotheses, with overlapping prior cohorts, no demonstrated causal mechanism and no established clinical utility.
ai_technology: Cox LASSO prognostic scoring
organization: Loudi Central Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary publisher PDF: abstract, cohort definitions, Cox-LASSO Methods, bootstrap/nested-CV Results, external evaluation and limitations; publisher-deposited date metadata.

title: PLS-DA nominates exploratory serum-metabolite patterns in osteopenia
summary: Supervised PLS-DA and model-derived VIP feature scores helped nominate serum-metabolite patterns across bone-density groups in 220 adults. The study reported 30, 55 and 49 exploratory candidates for osteopenia versus controls, osteoporosis versus controls and osteoporosis versus osteopenia, using seven-fold cross-validation and permutation checks. All selected metabolites had FDR-adjusted q values above 0.05 and were retained under exploratory VIP, nominal-P and fold-change thresholds. The 135-person discovery and 85-person temporal replication groups came from one hospital; these findings do not establish prospective fracture prediction, external transport or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA)

title: IceCube DeepCore data constrain long-range neutrino interactions
summary: First located in an arXiv version posted January 3, 2026, this study received a journal version on November 20 with revised event-score bins. It uses trained boosted-decision-tree scores from IceCube’s pre-applied classification pipeline to group released DeepCore events for oscillation fits. Analyzing eight years of atmospheric-neutrino data, the authors find no evidence for the tested long-range interactions and report constraints on their coupling strengths. The result depends on the specified physical hypotheses and experimental systematics; the classifier identifies event topology and was not newly trained by these authors.

title: Human-trained neural model predicts regulatory maps across 447 mammalian genomes
summary: Using an experimentally mapped human atlas of 5.33 million regulatory elements from 4,159 samples, researchers trained a cell-context-informed neural sequence model. It predicted cell-selective accessibility, generalized to observed mouse data and was applied to predict regulatory activity across 447 mammalian genomes. The human atlas was measured experimentally, while the broad cross-species maps remain computational predictions without validation in every species. Zenodo metadata dates this preprint November 20, 2026; the version record was created November 21, which does not establish a November 20 archive posting.

title: AlphaFold homodimer predictions link truncation to different interface outcomes
summary: The May 9, 2026 preprint version compared 5,168 canonical/truncated human homodimer prediction pairs using AlphaFold-Multimer structures and interface-confidence scores. Among 234 pairs with high-confidence canonical homodimers, it classified 132 as conserved, 61 as interface-ablated and 41 as partially destabilized. These are computational classifications, without biochemical or cellular confirmation of the specific dimers. The later deposited abstract retains these headline proportions but revises interpretations of apparent interface emergence; those emergence and disorder claims are outside this entry.

title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in PARN-mutant zebrafish
summary: Researchers found expanded hematopoietic stem/progenitor populations and reduced mature blood cells in PARN-loss zebrafish; cholesterol-pathway inhibition rescued expansion and anemia, and cholesterol-pathway activation was also observed in patient-derived iPSCs. Ilastik interactive machine learning generated image probability maps, followed by CellProfiler/Otsu segmentation, to quantify blood-lineage staining and cell counts supporting the phenotype and treatment comparisons. This AI role concerned image-based measurement; pathway identification and rescue conclusions also relied on experimental and transcriptomic assays. The treatment findings remain preclinical, and the iPSC observations do not establish patient benefit.
ai_technology: Ilastik interactive machine learning for bioimage analysis
organization: CHEO Research Institute; University of Ottawa

title: Predicted enzyme structures support shared substrate gates in C-glycosylation
summary: Analysis of structural models for 56 C-active UGT enzymes found acceptor gates throughout the set and two enzymes lacking a discernible donor gate; AlphaFold3 and source-labeled RobettaFold models supported variable open/closed gate conformations. These predictions extended a gating hypothesis derived from experimental structures and molecular simulations, rather than independently measuring dynamics across all enzymes. For maize ZmUGT708A6, crystallography, biochemical/mutational tests and QM/MM calculations supported a stepwise C-glycosylation mechanism involving water-mediated stabilization of a high-energy sigma complex. The AI contribution concerns comparison of predicted gate architectures; direct mechanistic tests focused on selected enzymes and substrates.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3; RobettaFold
organization: Freie Universität Berlin; Technical University of Denmark

source_review.scope: Publisher article abstract; selected gate-architecture and reaction-mechanism Results; computational/crystallographic Methods; contributions and affiliations. Supplementary model-generation material was not reviewed.

title: Neural-potential simulations clarify a phosphonium/HFIP catalyst for CO2 conversion
summary: Researchers synthesized phosphonium-salt/HFIP catalysts for converting CO2 and epoxides into cyclic carbonates, reporting yields of 86–96% for monosubstituted and 66–88% for disubstituted epoxides at 25 °C and 1 atm CO2. Matlantis PFP v5.0.0, a trained neural interatomic potential, sampled the liquid-mixture structure; radial-distribution analysis supported strong association between HFIP and bromide. The calculated density differed from experiment by about 5%, while NMR and conventional DFT calculations provided complementary structural/mechanistic evidence. AI supported characterization of the new catalytic system; catalyst preparation and performance were experimentally established.
ai_technology: Matlantis Preferred Potential Framework (PFP) v5.0.0, TeaNet-inspired neural network interatomic potential
organization: University of Alicante; University of Almería; University of Salerno; University of Camerino

title: Sonopet aspirates support genomic and epigenomic profiling of skull-base meningioma
summary: In a prospectively collected paired feasibility series of seven patients, Sonopet aspirate and standard-resection skull-base meningioma specimens produced comparable sequencing yield, read quality and tumor purity. Copy-number profiles were highly concordant (Lin’s CCC0.99;95% CI0.76–1.00), whereas somatic variant-burden agreement was weaker and imprecise (CCC0.53;95% CI−0.28–0.99); promoter methylation was closely correlated. Learned Dorado models interpreted nanopore sequence/modified-base signals, and the ClairS-TO neural ensemble called somatic variants for the comparison. This small specimen-feasibility study, partly funded by Stryker, does not establish improved patient outcomes or independent replication.
ai_technology: Dorado high-accuracy and modified-base models; ClairS-TO trained neural-network ensemble
organization: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center; Mayo Clinic

title: Physics-informed neural model predicts cervical cancer progression in retrospective cohorts
summary: Researchers at Vellore Institute of Technology report a physics-informed neural model for two-year progression-free survival prediction in cervical cancer, evaluated retrospectively in a 20,287-patient analytical cohort and two external Indian cohorts totaling 15,967 patients. The abstract reports internal time-dependent AUC 0.91 and external AUCs 0.87 and 0.86; the 2,663-patient 2023 temporal subset is included within the 3,043-patient held-out test set. Model-derived clusters with differing survival outcomes remain hypotheses requiring prospective validation. This source check covers the publisher abstract and publication metadata; it does not establish prospective patient benefit or causal biological mechanisms.

title: Random forest classifies eight infant illnesses in a retrospective Bangladesh dataset
summary: A Daffodil International University study compares four supervised models on 2,552 infant health records covering eight illness categories, assembled from hospital records and caregiver reports in Bangladesh. The publisher abstract reports 99.22% accuracy and 99.04% macro F1 for an optimized random forest using a stratified 80:20 split, with cross-validation, bootstrap and calibration analyses. These are retrospective internal evaluation results; clinical deployment, independent external validation and improved caregiver or patient outcomes are not established by the reviewed abstract. This source check covers the publisher abstract and metadata.

title: Machine learning and cell assays prioritize FASN in a smoking–male-infertility study
summary: Researchers at Meishan City Second People’s Hospital integrated three infertility transcriptomic datasets with network toxicology and used LASSO and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination to prioritize candidate genes. The publisher abstract reports a genetic association between higher predicted FASN expression and male-infertility risk and increased FASN mRNA after cigarette-smoke-condensate exposure in mouse TM4 Sertoli cells. These findings nominate FASN for functional investigation; they do not show that FASN mediates smoke-induced reproductive injury or establish a treatment. This source check covers the publisher abstract, affiliations and publication metadata; full methods were not assessed.

title: Vocabulary app with Qwen tutoring shows a short-term score advantage in eight classes
summary: A twelve-week teaching study randomized four matched pairs of university tutorial classes to a vocabulary application or non-adaptive word lists. The application bundled Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct examples, wav2vec2.0 pronunciation feedback and rule-based review scheduling. Among 92 completers from 100 allocated students, class-adjusted posttest scores favored the application by 6.6 points on a 100-point test (95% CI 1.3–11.9). This is a prospective comparison of the complete instructional package, not an isolated effect of AI. Eight classes, repeated test items, complete-case analysis and no delayed-retention measure limit generalization.

title: EEG–fMRI feature fusion distinguishes CELF-defined language difficulty in a retrospective cohort
summary: Pairwise learned classifiers fused EEG microstate and fMRI-connectivity features to distinguish CELF-defined language difficulty from controls in 173 participants. The authors report 78.4% balanced accuracy under nested cross-validation with training-only feature selection. This is within-cohort discrimination, not a prospective screening result or evidence of a causal language mechanism. SHAP interpretation used an original non-nested model rather than the most frequent nested classifier. The main Methods body and complete fMRI preprocessing were unavailable in the reviewed publisher snapshot; subgroup counts do not fully describe the 173-person sample.

title: Sensor LSTM predicts part dimensions in an injection-molding campaign
summary: A shared bidirectional LSTM with four regression heads predicted weight and dimensions from injection-molding sensor sequences. The campaign collected 132 molding cycles, with 124 retained for regression. On a selected 24-cycle comparison subset, the model reported average MAPE 0.27%. This is an evaluation on the study’s campaign, with epoch selection using held-out folds. Comparators used different evaluation units and protocols, so the reported errors do not establish general model superiority. Generalization across molds, materials, machines and production periods remains untested.
ai_technology: Bidirectional LSTM shared encoder with task-specific MLP regression heads
organization: Clemson University; University of Delaware; University of South Carolina

title: Machine learning prioritizes blood markers associated with neuralgia and depressive symptoms
summary: LASSO and random forest prioritized four blood-expression markers shared by postherpetic-neuralgia and depression datasets. A separate 240-person clinical study found higher candidate-marker expression in neuralgia with depressive symptoms; serum LTF/sCD40L discrimination had AUC 0.818 within the 120 neuralgia patients. Symptoms were defined by PHQ-9 rather than a formal psychiatric interview. These are candidate associations, not a causal pain–depression mechanism or validated clinical diagnosis. The public-data four-gene model was refitted in its comparison cohort, so it was not fixed-coefficient external validation.

title: Machine-learning feature selection prioritizes two coronary-disease-associated genes
summary: XGBoost, SVM recursive feature elimination and Boruta narrowed transcriptomic candidates to DYRK2 and SIGIRR, whose expression was lower in coronary heart disease. The study analyzed 141 discovery samples and 24 samples in a second public dataset, then confirmed lower expression in newly collected clinical samples from 5 patients and 5 controls. Both public datasets informed final gene selection, so the second dataset was not an untouched diagnostic test. Single-cell associations were exploratory; the work establishes neither causal gene roles nor clinical diagnostic utility.

title: Inverse optimal control infers shared and patient-specific squat objectives after knee replacement
summary: Bi-level inverse optimal control inferred individual and shared movement-objective weights from recorded squats in six people after total knee replacement. Center-of-mass height and balance were dominant fitted terms, while balance weights varied across subjects; these are model-dependent inferences rather than direct measurements of neural control. The June 15, 2026 preprint reported within-sample trajectory reconstructions. A November 22 revision added leave-one-subject-out testing within the same six-person dataset, reporting mean RMSE 7.36° and correlation 0.95. Neither version establishes prediction from preoperative data, external-cohort generalization or improved clinical outcomes.

title: A Bayesian nonparametric model identifies short-lived frequency-selective states in motor-cortex MEG
summary: A Bayesian nonparametric mixture model inferred brief frequency-selective activity states in a public resting-state MEG dataset from one left motor-cortex parcel. The first preprint version, posted December 23, 2025, reported two aperiodic and five oscillatory states with marked variation in occupancy, frequency and power across people. Its Methods and Results disagree on whether the cohort contained 64 or 65 participants. A June 2026 revision retained the broad state decomposition but changed numerical frequency estimates; the November 2026 abstract retains the broad finding. These are model-inferred signal patterns, without independent neural-state ground truth, external replication or demonstrated behavioral/clinical meaning.

title: Transformer-assisted bibliometric analysis maps changes in Italian computer science
summary: A study combined learned co-authorship and text representations with topic clustering to analyze a roster of 1,229 Italian computer-science scholars and publication records from 1980–2025. It identified three model-derived periods spanning foundational work, computer vision/machine learning, and later applied AI/health informatics. An ancillary Genoa pilot introduced 15 recommended researcher pairs, with four joint projects reported within six months. The topic patterns depend on metadata and analytical thresholds, 44.2% of paper abstracts were missing, and the small uncontrolled pilot does not establish a causal collaboration benefit.

title: A retrospective prostate-cancer messaging study finds different strengths in GPT-4 and clinician replies
summary: A retrospective study compared clinical-team replies with a GPT-4-based bot for 158 prostate-cancer patient inquiries. Clinicians rated team replies higher on completeness, correctness and clarity, while bot replies scored higher on empathy and more often required major editing. Four LLM graders favored bot replies and showed lower inter-grader agreement than clinician graders. The reviewed publisher abstract describes an evolving rubric and response-quality evaluation, without establishing patient outcomes, prospective workflow utility or clinical safety effects; full Methods were inaccessible.

title: Imbalance-aware modelling identifies severe-crash patterns in Selangor records
summary: A study used Random Forest, XGBoost and SVM to analyze 6,978 fatal or serious crash reports from Selangor, Malaysia, covering 2012–2020,with one stratified 70:30 split and training-only class balancing. The selected class-weighted Random Forest had 81.66% accuracy but only 20.53% recall and 30.10% precision for serious crashes. Tree-model feature importance emphasized collision type, while other rankings varied by model; low-capacity motorcycle involvement was described separately through record frequencies. The dataset excludes minor-injury crashes and lacks exposure denominators, so these associations do not establish causality, population risk or transfer beyond one state and split.

title: Machine learning reveals distinct neural control of morning and evening body-temperature rhythms in Drosophila
summary: The February 2026 THERM-D preprint used learned fly localization in camera images to track temperature-preference rhythms over several days. Body temperature was inferred from flies’ positions on a temperature gradient, rather than directly measured by thermal imaging, and targeted genetic perturbations implicated CRYPTOCHROME-negative clock neurons in the morning temperature rise without the same evening effect. Author-maintained software documents a trained YOLOv8 object detector supporting fly localization. These are Drosophila findings, not an established human mechanism; the later November 2026 journal version is distinct from the preprint summarized here.

title: Learned wing sensing supports damage detection and lift recovery in a flapping robot
summary: A prototype flapping-wing robot used integrated wing sensors with a learned Kriging surrogate to reconstruct wing motion and a linear SVM to classify damaged states. The SVM achieved 94.6% accuracy on 168 held-out samples, and a separate damaged-wing bench demonstration increased flapping frequency within 0.1 seconds to restore average lift near the intact baseline. These are device-specific physical sensing and control results, with calibration and comparison against binocular-vision measurements. They do not establish autonomous free-flight performance, generalization across robot designs or sustained field operation.

summary: XGBoost and four feature-importance analyses characterized EEG differences between focused-attention meditation and instructed mind-wandering in 26 experienced meditators. summary: In 3,092 hypertensive CHARLS participants followed for a median eight years, a preprint compared learned cardiovascular-event predictors using baseline risk factors. Interpreted neural networks flag candidate schizophrenia loci in the Estonian Biobank
summary: Feedforward neural networks trained on genome-wide genotypes of 1,814 schizophrenia cases and 7,325 matched controls from the Estonian Biobank were interpreted post hoc (integrated gradients, with permuted-label models to estimate P-values) to flag potentially associated loci. One locus passed the strict threshold and seven loci (14 SNPs) the relaxed threshold, in regions not identified by the authors' linear baseline; the strongest overlaps a known bipolar-disorder locus. Only 6, 3 or 1 of 1,370 previously established schizophrenia loci were recovered, depending on the overlap rule. The authors report concordance with schizophrenia and bipolar-disorder loci and brain-related enrichment, but P-values were not well calibrated in a small type 1 diabetes test, no uncertainty quantification or ground truth exists, and replication in other populations and biobanks is still needed. The flagged loci are statistical candidates, not validated associations or treatment targets. This is primarily a method paper; the earlier arXiv preprint (2024) did not contain the schizophrenia analysis, so the journal version is dated.

title: Machine learning links a plasma protein signature to symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection

A score from the signature was associated with acute symptom burden, disease severity and post-COVID sequelae, and higher pre-infection HDL concentrations were inversely associated with it. The authors note that feature selection was performed outside the cross-validation folds, so discrimination may be optimistic, that the signature lacks external validation, and that post-COVID symptoms were self-reported.

The authors state that the two methods used different input data, so the gain reflects both the information in notes and the model; this is a single-health-system proof of concept in a preprint.

title: Machine learning prioritises osteoarthritis genes tested under macrophage stretch
summary: Random forest ranking and LASSO regression narrowed a 168-gene synovial co-expression module to five candidates (E2F3, C6orf211, NDUFC2, SPCS2, DOCK10) using public datasets (discovery 29 normal and 30 osteoarthritis samples; auxiliary GSE89408 with 28 and 22). The combined score reached AUC 0.817 in discovery and 0.797 in the auxiliary cohort. In LPS-activated RAW264.7 macrophages (six biological replicates per group), cyclic stretch lowered E2F3, SPCS2 and DOCK10 and raised NDUFC2 relative to LPS alone, alongside lower inflammatory readouts. The authors note the auxiliary cohort also informed selection and is not independent validation, the sample is small, the cell line is murine, there was no stretch-only or time-course control, and the LPS-induced E2F3 protein increase was not significant.

title: Multimodal machine learning prioritizes candidate inhibitors of giant cancer cells
summary: A multimodal ensemble combining chemical fingerprints, drug-induced cell morphology, transcriptomic perturbation profiles and biological annotations was trained on screening data from four breast cancer cell lines, reaching mean Pearson correlation 0.403 and recovering 27.9% of experimentally identified hits in held-out screening data. Evidence is limited to cell lines and modest predictive accuracy, selectivity against normal cells was not read, and the preprint is not peer reviewed.

title: Deep learning scores Claudin18.2 staining in gastric cancer slides across clones
summary: A pipeline that scores Claudin18.2 immunohistochemistry on whole-slide images used a LoRA-adapted UNI pathology foundation model for tumour recognition, adapter-based staining-intensity classification and two rounds of active learning. In a non-randomised reader study, AI assistance improved every pathologist's agreement with the reference standard and shortened review time. The authors state the study is single-centre with limited prospective and cross-clone cohorts, uses expert consensus rather than absolute ground truth, may propagate errors across modules, and provides no treatment-response or outcome data; at the 50% cutoff the retrospective AUC was lower than one pathologist's.

title: Deep learning predicts DNA damage response protein levels from routine slides
summary: Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning on frozen pathology foundation-model tile embeddings predicted reverse-phase protein array pathway scores from 1,673 TCGA haematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images covering 1,527 patients with breast, endometrial, cervical and ovarian cancer and uterine carcinosarcoma. Cross-validation was cancer-type-stratified and site-grouped. This is a moderate retrospective association in one public cohort: there is no external validation, no clinical or treatment-response outcome, and the authors list separating the signal from proliferation as future work, noting the cell-cycle score was predicted more strongly.

title: Machine learning forecasts acute food crises and separates predictive from causal drivers
summary: Missing-data-resilient machine-learning pipelines, including gradient boosting and a tabular foundation model, forecast acute food crisis occurrence 3, 6 and 9 months ahead across 80 countries using monthly subnational data for 2007-2024, exceeding no-skill baselines by 15 to 50 percentage points in PR-AUC under nested cross-validation. TreeSHAP profiles fell into three recurring archetypes. Doubly robust causal estimates indicated that acute conflict events, which carried the weakest predictive signal, are primary causal drivers, while agroclimatology was the only dimension where predictive and causal importance agreed. The authors report that skill tracks crisis prevalence, that the causal effects are modest and only moderately robust to unmeasured confounding, and that they depend on an assumed causal graph; several variables were reported as non-identifiable. The work is a preprint.
ai_technology: Tree-based and tabular foundation-model classifiers with TreeSHAP attribution and cross-fitted doubly robust causal estimation.

title: Generative AI designs Type I photosensitizers tested in cells and mice
summary: A cross-attention classifier trained on 1,338 curated photosensitizers (85.8% accuracy and ROC-AUC 0.918 on a scaffold split) and an RNN scaffold-decorating generator proposed candidates on a redesigned tetracyclic scaffold. Six were synthesised and all produced superoxide under light. The lead compound had IC50 3.3 micromolar in 4T1 cells under normoxia and 4.5 micromolar at 2% oxygen, with similar values in HepG2 and MCF-7, and markedly slowed 4T1 tumour growth in mice over 14 days with four animals per group. Validation covers one scaffold and six molecules, the lead was also phototoxic to normal HUVEC cells (IC50 3.5 micromolar under normoxia), hypoxia attenuated but did not abolish its effect, and the in vivo group size was small.

title: Deep learning EEG metric linked to mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
summary: A deep-learning model trained on 22,044 polysomnography recordings estimated the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel, correlating r=0.88 with the scored index in internal testing and r=0.50 to 0.62 in three external test sets. Two derived metrics, the discrepancy between the EEG-based and scored index and an estimate from epochs without scored respiratory events, were associated with all-cause and non-cardiovascular mortality among participants free of cardiovascular disease after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors; the event-free estimate was also associated with cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest quartile. Data came from the KISS, MESA, MrOS and SHHS cohorts. The findings are retrospective associations in a preprint, external agreement is weaker, hazard ratios and per-cohort sizes were not reviewed, and the authors suggest the discrepancy is not solely model error.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model estimates the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel; derived discrepancy metrics are tested against mortality.

title: LLM-agent workflow reports new proofs on positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics
summary: A preprint describes PatternMiner, in which an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets, trains small models (MLPs, small transformers, trees), interprets them and formulates conjectures that are tested against counterexamples in mathematical software, applied to five positivity problems from Stanley's survey. The paper gives proofs, labelled LLM-generated, that for every n>=5 no fixed number of retained flag dimensions suffices for projection tests of Schubert structure-constant vanishing, an equivariant positivity inequality that proves Conjectures A and B of Chen et al. on equivariant nonvanishing, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted case of Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorial invariance, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients, supported by finite checks such as 776,891 coefficients over 1,587 shape instances. Proofs received an internal adversarial review only; no proof-kernel or independent mathematician check is reported, one decisive construction needed human redirection, and the comparison with direct LLM attempts is not compute-matched.
ai_technology: Unnamed LLM agent that trains and interprets small models (activation patching, probes, sparse autoencoders), proposes conjectures and attempts proofs, with counterexample searches in mathematical software.
organization: University of Washington; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

title: Satellite machine learning measures inundation across 542,850 conserved wetland sites
summary: A Support Vector Machine classifier applied to Sentinel-2 and Dynamic World data in Google Earth Engine mapped surface-water inundation across 542,850 wetland-related Conservation Reserve Program and Wetlands Reserve Program sites from 2018 to 2024.
