title: AI-measured retinal vessel metrics nominally linked to cognitive impairment in diabetes
summary: In 630 community-dwelling adults with type 2 diabetes from four Guiyang health centres, the EVision AI system quantified retinal vascular density and fractal dimensions from fundus photographs. Mild cognitive impairment by MoCA-B affected 33.2% (n=209); after adjustment, vascular density (OR 0.987 per 1%), fractal dimension (OR 0.221 per 0.1, 95% CI 0.050-0.982) and vessel-centerline fractal dimension (OR 0.359 per 0.1) were nominally associated with lower odds, with consistent directions across age and diabetes-duration strata; sensitivity analyses supported only vascular density and centerline fractal dimension. The design is cross-sectional with MoCA-B screening rather than diagnosis, 132 participants were excluded (117 for image failure), and the associations are exploratory and not causal.

title: Unsupervised clustering splits Ethiopian rainfall into ten seasonal regimes

Agreement between the two clustering methods was checked monthly with the Adjusted Rand Index. Earlier station-based studies proposed five to eight zones; this preprint reports no validation against independent station records or forecasts, so the regimes are descriptive and not yet shown to improve forecasting or planning.

title: Machine learning selects an exploratory mitochondrial gene signature in diabetic retinopathy
summary: Differential expression, GSEA and WGCNA on two GEO diabetic retinopathy datasets (GSE102485, GSE60436) yielded 13 core mitochondria-related genes; LASSO regression and SVM-RFE selected a five-gene diagnostic model (CKMT1A, SLC25A27, SHMT2, ALDH1L1, CYCS) with a mean AUC of 0.89 in internal 10-fold cross-validation. title: Machine learning prioritises KHDC4, tested as a colon cancer driver in cells and mice
summary: Single-cell RNA-seq differential expression and univariate Cox screening on TCGA colon adenocarcinoma (428 patients) were followed by several machine learning methods (including LASSO, Boruta, random survival forests and XGBoost), whose intersection gave five prognostic genes; KHDC4 contributed across all algorithms. KHDC4 was higher in 50 paired tumour samples and linked to lymph node metastasis and stage; knockdown reduced proliferation and metastasis in HT29/HCT116 cells and in nude-mouse xenograft and liver-metastasis models (n=5 per group). RIP and fractionation suggest KHDC4 binds E2F3 mRNA and promotes its nuclear export. Limits stated by the authors: the scRNA-seq discovery used one paired patient sample, the export machinery is unresolved, antiproliferative effects may confound invasion assays, and no external prognostic cohort was used.

title: Machine learning selects cell-death genes in COPD tested with an herbal formula in rats
summary: Mendelian randomization screened 439 programmed-cell-death genes with genetic causal links to COPD; intersection with transcriptomic and co-expression analyses and several machine-learning algorithms selected five diagnostic markers (NT5E, SPP1, BLK, PLAT, LGMN). Single-cell analysis and virtual perturbation suggested a bidirectional role for LGMN. In a rat COPD model, the traditional Chinese medicine formula Feizhangning dose-dependently lowered IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha in serum and lavage fluid and reversed the abnormal mRNA and protein expression of the five genes. This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint; docking and network pharmacology are computational, diagnostic performance and animal numbers were not reviewed, and no human test is reported.

title: Independent UK test of eight mammography AI algorithms as second reader and triage
summary: Eight commercial deep learning breast cancer detection algorithms from five vendors were evaluated retrospectively on 22,778 mammograms from two UK screening sites (Cambridge, Norwich; 2017) with 3-year follow-up. Standalone AUCs ranged 0.82-0.91, with one algorithm inferior to all others. Paired with the first human reader, all but one were noninferior in sensitivity to double reading (64.7-67.4% vs 67.9%) with superior specificity (97.5% vs 97.1%); low-suspicion triage ruled out 37.4-65.7% of mammograms while missing at most 1.0% of screen-detected cancers. Gains came with more arbitration, and the study is retrospective; prospective workflow effects were not measured.

title: Machine learning picks AgCuTi wetting conditions on WCu that experiments confirm
summary: Eight regression models were trained on 125 full-factorial wetting experiments varying temperature, titanium content and surface roughness; the best, a support vector regressor (held-out R2 0.945), screened 37,572 candidate conditions and selected 10 representative ones. Experiments at those conditions matched predicted contact angles with a mean absolute error of 0.55 degrees (R2 0.91). A second gradient-boosting model with SHAP attributed about 70% of the contribution to the three process variables, with post-wetting morphology adding correlational information. This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint from a single laboratory and a narrow design space.

title: Machine learning classifier on salivary-gland transcriptomes separates Sjogren disease
summary: Bulk RNA-seq of salivary-gland tissue from 98 primary Sjogren disease patients and 22 controls was used to compare 14 machine-learning algorithms on 193 candidate genes; CatBoost performed best, with an AUC of 0.981 on pooled external GEO tissue datasets (218 patients, 32 controls). Network analysis, not the model, prioritized LCP2, PTPRC and ZAP70, which SHAP ranked among the top features; multiplex immunohistochemistry in 5 patients and 5 controls showed higher protein expression. Blood performance was modest, specificity versus other autoimmune diseases was only preliminary, and the authors note two of the genes were reported before and that prospective multicentre validation is needed.

title: Machine learning prioritizes exploratory angiogenesis genes in endometriosis endometrium
summary: Transcriptomic analysis of eutopic endometrium (GEO GSE51981) found 238 angiogenesis-related differentially expressed genes in endometriosis; LASSO and random forest, combined with WGCNA, prioritized COL6A1, ERN2 and IL34, and the selected random forest reached an AUC of 0.806 on a second dataset (GSE23339). ERN2 and IL34 differed between groups in that dataset while COL6A1 did not. The work is purely computational: the authors call the cross-dataset AUC exploratory rather than independent validation, the findings do not extend to ectopic lesions, and compound prioritization, docking and dynamics are hypothesis-generating only.
